subsystems.name: Biometric sensing
subsystems.role: measure the body signals the system would react to.
parts: optional ambient camera or microphone for behaviour

subsystems.name: Stress inference
subsystems.role: turn noisy physiology into a usable estimate of arousal or stress.
parts: personal baseline model (each person differs widely)
motion and context filters to reject artefacts
classifier trained on labelled stress data
uncertainty estimate, so the system knows when it is guessing

subsystems.name: Environment actuators
subsystems.role: the things that can actually be changed in a room.
parts: tunable LED lighting (colour temperature and brightness)
active noise masking and soundscape speakers
radiant panels or local heaters for fast response

subsystems.name: Control loop
subsystems.role: decide what to change, by how much, and when to stop.
parts: rate limiting so the room does not flicker and swing
logging of what worked for whom

subsystems.name: Data and privacy layer
subsystems.role: keep continuous physiological data safe and consented.

buildSteps.title: Choose the stress signal
buildSteps.detail: Cortisol is a hormone, not a mood: it follows a daily rhythm and rises over minutes to tens of minutes, so it cannot drive a fast control loop. A practical design leans on heart-rate variability and skin conductance for moment-to-moment arousal, and uses cortisol only as a slow trend.

buildSteps.title: Build the sensor
buildSteps.detail: For a wearable, that means a skin-contact patch with electrodes and a small electrochemical cell that detects cortisol in sweat, plus standard optical heart-rate sensing. Calibration against blood or saliva samples is needed per person.

buildSteps.title: Collect labelled data
buildSteps.detail: Volunteers are monitored during controlled stressful and calm tasks, indoors and outdoors, at different times of day, so the model learns what is stress and what is merely coffee, cold or exercise.

buildSteps.title: Train a personal model
buildSteps.detail: Because absolute hormone and heart-rate values vary enormously between people, the system learns each user's baseline and flags deviations from it, rather than using one global threshold.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the room
buildSteps.detail: Dimmable, colour-tunable lights, motorised blinds, masking speakers and zoned HVAC are fitted with a common control interface and given known response times.

buildSteps.title: Write the control policy
buildSteps.detail: Rules or a learned controller map a stress estimate to small environmental changes - warmer colour temperature, quieter masking, a one-degree temperature nudge - with smoothing so the room changes gradually.

buildSteps.title: Run closed-loop trials
buildSteps.detail: The system is tested against a sham control (identical room, no response) to check whether measured stress or reported comfort actually improves, not just whether the sensors fire.

buildSteps.title: Validate and constrain
buildSteps.detail: Energy use, comfort for other occupants and failure modes are checked; the user can always override, and the system is disabled if its estimate is uncertain.

prerequisites.why: sweat and interstitial-fluid cortisol sensors work in the lab but drift, need calibration and have not been shown reliable for everyday wear.

prerequisites.tech: Wearable stress detection from heart-rate variability
prerequisites.why: consumer devices estimate arousal reasonably well on average but are poor for individuals, which is what a personal control loop needs.

prerequisites.tech: Personal thermal and lighting comfort models
prerequisites.why: comfort varies by person and activity; models that predict an individual's preference are improving but not yet dependable.
tunable LEDs, variable-speed heat pumps and zoned ventilation already respond in seconds to minutes.
physiological signals can be processed locally, which is the only credible way to deploy continuous monitoring.

pathway.milestone: wearables that flag likely stress and suggest a break or a breathing exercise
rooms that adapt to occupancy and measured arousal, tested against sham controls in offices and classrooms
pathway.unlocks: evidence on whether environmental change actually lowers stress.

pathway.milestone: reliable multi-signal stress estimation and calibrated wearable cortisol trend sensing
pathway.unlocks: a trustworthy trigger signal for automation.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop personal environments that learn each occupant's preferences and share a room fairly
pathway.unlocks: buildings that adjust themselves to the people inside, with energy use and privacy kept in check.
